page: Vultr vcg-a40-1c-5g-2vram is a fractional GPU instance within the Cloud GPU family. It features a single dedicated Intel x86_64 vCPU operating at 2.0 GHz, with one physical core and one thread. The system is equipped with 5.0 GB of system memory and 90 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Acceleration is provided by a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU, delivering 2 GB of dedicated VRAM, which represents approximately 0.0417 of a full A40 GPU.

Performance benchmarks indicate a stark contrast between general-purpose compute and GPU-accelerated workloads. The single-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1713.88 and a gzip compression throughput of 27.42 GB/sec. However, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations score in the bottom 10% due to the single-core limitation and weak memory subsystem. Conversely, the fractional GPU configuration excels at lightweight AI tasks, achieving top-tier performance in LLM inference for a small 135M model, with prompt processing at 9931.92 tokens/sec and text generation at 454.57 tokens/sec. It also demonstrates strong prompt processing performance of 211.23 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model.

This instance offers a highly cost-efficient entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads by slicing a high-end NVIDIA A40 GPU into a smaller, fractional resource. This resource density allows users to access Ampere-generation hardware without paying for a full GPU. However, the tradeoff is a highly constrained CPU and memory profile, which limits its suitability for general-purpose computing, database hosting, or high-throughput web serving. The instance is best suited for small-scale LLM inference, lightweight machine learning model testing, and basic GPU-accelerated development tasks.
